population: US cities, Mexican peso-crisis inflow, low-skill
outcome: native low-skill wages; rents; long-run housing
estimate: short run wages down and rents up; long run lower house prices where immigrants enter construction
text: In the short run, high-immigration locations see their low-skilled labor force increase, native low-skilled wages decrease, and the relative price of rentals increase. ... lasting consequences are a) worse labor market conditions for low-skilled natives who entered the labor force in high-immigration years, and b) lower housing prices in high-immigrant locations

estimate: crowd-out in nontradable immigrant-intensive jobs; no such effect across tradable occupations
text: a local influx of immigrants crowds out employment of native-born workers in more relative to less immigrant-intensive nontradable jobs, but has no such effect across tradable occupations

population: US and Canada, native men, skill cells
estimate: Sub-sample 2SLS elasticities average around minus one
text: For U.S. and Canada, Sub-Sample 2SLS elasticities average around minus one, very stable across alternative specifications and different instruments.

estimate: low-skill immigrant presence with losses at the bottom; foreign-born presence with gains at the top
text: an increased presence of low-skilled immigrants is associated with losses at the lower end of wage distribution ... the presence of foreign-born workers, whether high- or low-skilled, is associated with substantial gains for high-wage natives

estimate: +1.7 to +2.6% wages of less-educated natives, 2000-2019; no significant wage effect on college-educated natives; positive employment-rate effect
text: immigration ... had a positive and significant effect between +1.7 to +2.6% on wages of less educated native workers, over the period 2000-2019 and no significant wage effect on college educated natives. We also calculate a positive employment rate effect for most native workers.

population: US firms in the 2021-22 H-2B lottery, low-skill nonfarm
estimate: production elasticity 0.20-0.22; investment 1.5-2.1; profit rate 0.15; native employment zero or positive
text: Firms exogenously authorized to employ more immigrants in low-skill jobs significantly increase production (elasticity 0.20–0.22), investment (1.5–2.1), and the rate of profit (0.15). ... the effect on native employment is zero or positive overall, and positive in rural areas.

population: undocumented vs legal immigrants, not vs US-born
estimate: unadjusted gap over 35%; male penalty about 4% in 2016 after observables
text: the unadjusted gap in the log hourly wage between the average undocumented and legal immigrant is very large (over 35%), almost all of this gap disappears once the calculation adjusts for differences in observable socioeconomic characteristics. The wage penalty to undocumented immigration for men was only about 4% in 2016.

population: unauthorized worker flows, US local markets, early 2021 to early 2024
outcome: employment, wages, house prices, rents, transfers
estimate: employment +0.96% per 1% of initial employment; wages about -1 and imprecise; house prices +2.2%; rents +1.4%; transfers -4.5%
text: an increase in UIWF equal to 1% of initial employment increases local employment by 0.96% ... effect of UIWF on average weekly wages is roughly -1, but is imprecisely estimated. ... increased local house prices by 2.2% and increased local rents by 1.4%. ... reduction in government transfers of -4.5%

population: Bracero exclusion, Mexican farm workers, US states
estimate: fail to reject zero labor-market impact
text: We fail to reject zero labor market impact, inconsistent with this model.

estimate: -10% Hispanic students within 2 years; more than 300,000 displaced before 2012; no effect on non-Hispanic enrollment
text: local ICE partnerships reduce the number of Hispanic students by 10% within 2 years. We estimate partnerships enacted before 2012 displaced more than 300,000 Hispanic students.

population: US spatial model, skill-selective policy counterfactual
estimate: gains for low-skill workers, losses for high-skill workers, larger for incumbent high-skill immigrants
text: a skill selective immigration policy leads to welfare gains for low skill workers, but welfare losses for high skill workers. The negative impacts are more substantial among the incumbent high skill immigrants.

population: Mariel and other refugee waves, CPS subsamples
estimate: Mariel conflict is a Miami racial-composition break in small CPS cells; large losses for less-than-high-school workers not substantiated
text: contradictory findings on the effects of the Mariel Boatlift can be explained by a large difference in the pre- and post-Boatlift racial composition in certain very small subsamples ... fails to substantiate claims of large detrimental effects on workers with less than a high school education.

population: ICE arrest surge, Trump second term, local areas
outcome: work of likely undocumented; US-born employment
estimate: US-born employment-rate point estimates negative and not significant; rules out gains above 0.3 percentage points in impacted sectors; male employment rate -2.8 and -3.5 percentage points
text: The point estimates on the overall U.S.-born employment rate are negative, but not statistically significant; we rule out increases in likely impacted sectors of more than 0.3 percentage points ... a significant reduction in the male employment rate of 2.8 and 3.5 percentage points, across all and high-impact sectors, respectively.

paper: Amuedo-Dorantes Arenas-Arroyo Mahajan Schmidpeter IZA DP 16438
estimate: higher revenue and survival; no crowd-out of other employment; no negative competitor spillover
text: access to H-2B workers raises firms’ annual revenues and survival likelihood without crowding out other forms of employment. We do not find evidence of negative spillover effects on competitor firms.
